reason: The text contains multiple regular human characters who demonstrate clear agency throughout the narrative. The mother of Moses deliberately hides the child and takes action to place him in a waterproof basket and set it on the river (וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת־ הַיֶּ֔לֶד). His sister actively monitors the situation (וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה). Most notably, the sister takes initiative to approach Pharaoh's daughter with a proposal (וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל־ בַּת־ פַּרְעֹה), and Pharaoh's daughter herself shows agency by deciding to keep the child (וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו). These are not passive figures but active decision-makers driving the narrative forward.
